title: Arizona Tucson landmark model reference record
geometry: Official University of Arizona Planning Design and Construction ground-level GIS footprints; same campus transform as roads and terrain. Old Main body's cruciform polygon is not an outer veranda roofline. ENR2 consists of five ground-level polygons with open passages. McClelland Hall's courtyard opens south and is part of the concave outer ring.

sources.used: Inspected actual official exterior photo: rust-red central west entry tower, paired arched lights, mansard roof, small dormers, shaded wraparound pale wood veranda, masonry base and exterior staircase.
Inspected official entrance photograph and labelled floor plan. Brick wings, tall metal entrance columns, recessed gridded glass, open Witt courtyard. Distinct from McClelland Park.
Inspected official interior photograph: curved separate concrete volumes, five levels, rusted vertical fins, projecting open-air balconies, hanging vines, open canyon sky.
Confirms five-storey structure and open courtyard.

limitations: Floor heights, window placement, masonry colour, roof pitches, railing spacing and small landscape furniture are visual estimates, not measured surveys.

Old Main veranda is authored as an approximately 3.25-metre offset around the surveyed enclosed body; individual post positions are rhythmically spaced rather than matched to every tiny official column polygon.

ENR2 upper-storey balconies are interpretations of the official photo fitted to real ground-floor wings; upper-level outlines differ in reality. Only the ground canyon, not upper interior circulation, is presently playable.
Eller's interior rooms and building interior access are not implemented.
Downloaded photos are source references only. Runtime geometry uses original procedural surfaces rather than copying photo textures.
